examples.note: Partially legible in live play when players turn away or are mid-stride.
Strong in halftime walk-off close-up of Agüero.

assets.issues: Manchester City shirt-front sponsor. Usually excellent in close-ups and medium shots; weaker in fast live-play sequences when torsos are angled or distant. Poorer render example: 1433-1451s, where the logo drops to partially legible in motion.
assets.suggestions: Keep current high-contrast dark wordmark on sky blue, but add slightly thicker stroke/weight for long-lens live play. Favor tighter replay/cutaway framing after key actions to convert more live-play exposure into fully readable exposure.

examples.note: Board visible but secondary and less readable in fast, wide build-up.
Visit Etihad.com/Etihad reads well, but wide-angle distance limits impact versus close sideline shots.

assets.issues: Perimeter LED appears as ETIHAD / Etihad / Etihad.com / Visit Etihad.com. Generally readable, but often background-only in wide live-play angles. Dynamic camera pans reduce dwell time even when legible.
assets.suggestions: Increase dwell length on the ETIHAD creative rotation during sustained open play. Use fewer words per execution—prefer ETIHAD over URL-heavy variants in wide shots. Consider brighter board background or stronger outline to improve pickup at long camera distances.

examples.note: Dugout/bench branding is visible but secondary during Pep cutaway.
Fascia/dugout signage remains readable but background-only behind Pep.

assets.issues: Includes stadium fascia, stand, and dugout signage. Strong in bench/touchline cutaways and some wide stadium views; weaker only when relegated to background during manager shots.
assets.suggestions: This is already one of the better non-play surfaces. To lift value further, concentrate branding in the camera-facing dugout fascia and enlarge the wordmark on bench-seat blocks so touchline cutaways carry more dominant exposure.

brands.name: ETIHAD
brands.summary: Best-performing brand in the broadcast. Appears across shirt-front sponsor, perimeter LED, and stadium/dugout/fascia signage, with strongest exposure in close player shots and touchline cutaways.

examples.note: Sleeve reduces to logo-only visibility in live play.
Partially legible from behind Sané during score update.

assets.issues: Manchester City shirt-sleeve sponsor. Excellent in close throw-in and stoppage shots, especially 881-888s. Weakens in open play because the sleeve rotates away from camera and logo area is small.
assets.suggestions: Use a larger sleeve lockup and bolder letter spacing; current asset is clear in stills but loses authority in motion. A higher-contrast sleeve patch border would help when the arm is turned away from the lens.

examples.note: Visible in stoppage background but not dominant.
Readable behind touchline close-up, but still secondary.

assets.issues: Board creative is consistently legible, but usually background-secondary rather than hero exposure. Performs better in stoppages and throw-ins than in fluid central play.
assets.suggestions: Maintain the high-contrast board palette, but buy longer uninterrupted rotations near throw-ins/corners. If possible, simplify to the shortest brand form and avoid competing adjacency with other bright creatives.

brands.name: NEXEN TIRE
brands.summary: Strong overall. Sleeve placement delivers premium close-up exposure; LED exposure is solid but more background-dependent.

examples.note: Readable in wide live-play sequence, but small and backgrounded.
Late-game open-play exposure remains legible but not prominent.

assets.issues: Pitchside LED Nissan boards show repeatedly and remain readable, though mostly as wide-shot background media rather than focal branding.
assets.suggestions: Increase letter height and reduce negative space in the creative so the wordmark holds up better in high-wide angles. Pair rotations with dead-ball moments for longer dwell.

examples.note: Bench/fascia branding visible behind Pep but secondary.
Dugout branding present behind Klopp/Shaqiri substitution sequence, but not centered.

assets.issues: Appears on dugout/fascia/bench signage. Good non-play value in manager cutaways, but often partially occluded by bodies or shallow framing.
assets.suggestions: Excellent opportunity area: enlarge the dugout-facing Nissan mark and center it higher in the camera line so manager and substitute cutaways capture more uninterrupted exposure.

brands.name: Nissan
brands.summary: Good multi-surface visibility. Best value comes from non-play dugout/fascia exposure, with LED boards adding steady but mostly background impressions.

examples.note: Kit logo drops to logo-only visibility in live play.
Logo visible but small during moving player close-up.

assets.issues: Nike swoosh on Manchester City kit is crisp in stoppage close-up at 881-888s, but naturally small. It often resolves as logo-only rather than a strong brand impression during motion.
assets.suggestions: As a kit-manufacturer mark, size is the main constraint. For broadcast impact, a slightly larger chest swoosh or stronger contrast treatment would help. Supplement with more board creative near City attacking thirds.

examples.note: NIKE.COM/FOOTBALL is readable but long URL format reduces instant recognition in wide shot.
Nike.com/football clear, but still secondary in live attack sequence.

assets.issues: Board creative is legible, but URL-led copy is less efficient than a pure Nike brand mark in fast soccer coverage. Strong contrast; only real weakness is message complexity in wide shots.
assets.suggestions: Swap URL-heavy board creative for a larger swoosh + NIKE or a shorter football callout. The simpler lockup will read faster in panning open-play camera angles.

brands.name: Nike
brands.summary: Good but not dominant. The swoosh is clear when isolated, yet small; Nike’s board creative would benefit from simpler branding and less URL dependency.

examples.note: Visible in long midfield sequence but background-only for much of the run.
Present during replay package, but not the focal element.

assets.issues: AvaTrade boards are generally clean and readable, with strong color contrast. Main limitation is camera priority: the brand appears mostly as secondary backdrop during live play.
assets.suggestions: Very solid base creative. To improve return, secure more rotation share in stoppages, corners, and throw-ins where the board can sit longer in frame. Keep the bold brand name; avoid adding extra copy beyond one short tagline.

brands.name: AVATRADE
brands.summary: Strong creative fundamentals on LED boards, but exposure is mostly passive/background rather than hero-level.

examples.note: Readable in transition-wide shot but not held long enough to maximize impact.
Strong red-board contrast, though camera distance limits detail.

assets.issues: Aabar benefits from one of the best contrast profiles in the match: bright text against a saturated board. The weakness is not legibility but limited duration and background placement.
assets.suggestions: Lean into the high-contrast red execution—it works. Increase rotation frequency in attacking-third wide shots and hold the creative longer rather than swapping quickly.

brands.name: Aabar
brands.summary: Efficient LED creative with excellent contrast. Visibility is good whenever on screen, but total screen time looks limited.

examples.note: Readable in wide restart shot, but not large enough to dominate frame.
Visible during major Liverpool chance, but still a background board in fast action.

assets.issues: Appears as Abu Dhabi / Visit Abu Dhabi on perimeter LED. Good contextual exposure in live play, including a high-tension late chance, but mostly from wide angles where brand size is moderate.
assets.suggestions: Prefer the shortest brand form in fast live play and reserve 'Visit Abu Dhabi' for slower/stoppage phases. Larger type and fewer words would improve immediate read from the main camera.

brands.name: Abu Dhabi
brands.summary: Solid LED presence with decent contrast, but wide-angle framing and longer copy versions reduce impact.

examples.note: Replay segment contains Acronis board in background only; low focal priority.
Visible during Liverpool attack, but compressed by wide angle and motion.
Readable in open final-phase wide shot, but still secondary among multiple active brands.

assets.issues: Acronis is present on rotating perimeter LED, but mostly in wide or replay background. It is legible, yet less visually forceful than the highest-contrast board brands in this match.
assets.suggestions: Boost contrast and letter weight so the mark survives distant main-camera angles better. If possible, avoid cluttered adjacency with other bright board creatives and prioritize replay/stoppage rotations where the camera is steadier.

brands.name: Acronis
brands.summary: Visible but comparatively less commanding than other LED brands. Best fix is stronger creative contrast and better timing of board rotation.
